notes: A data-driven param is set from the cohort's own metadata, never a static default. Derive it, corroborate it against independent evidence in the SAME record, and STOP to ask when they conflict or the evidence is absent. A wrong value here does not error, it produces a confident wrong result.

seq_type corroboration is on the DNA/RNA axis, which is orthogonal to the TCR-vs-GEX labelling that was wrong in study 241114SHA (both TCR and GEX are RNA). The check is not there to re-catch that bug; it is there for a sample whose SequencingType says RNA but whose filename says WES.

ask.definition: The number of haplotypes in the combined FASTA: the distinct PanSN sample#haplotype prefixes of its sequence names (HG002#1 and HG002#2 are two; a haploid bacterial genome is one). pangenome 1.1.3 requires it and has no default; smoothxg and wfmash scale by it, so a wrong count gives a wrong graph without an error.
ask.on_conflict: The genome counts recorded for this file disagree. How many distinct sample#haplotype prefixes do its sequence names have?
ask.on_absent: Nothing in this assembly's metadata says how many genomes the combined FASTA holds. How many distinct PanSN sample#haplotype prefixes (sample#haplotype#contig) do its sequence names have?

ask.definition: Whether ESMFold folds the FASTA's chains together as one complex (multimer) or one at a time (monomer); a D.PSEQ with ChainCount 2 or more is a complex.
ask.on_conflict: The chain counts recorded for these sequences disagree. Is each FASTA one complex to fold together, or single chains?
ask.on_absent: not used: with no recorded chain count ESMFold keeps upstream's monomer default

ask.definition: Whether ColabFold folds the FASTA's chains together as one complex (alphafold2_multimer_v3) or one at a time (alphafold2_ptm); a D.PSEQ with ChainCount 2 or more is a complex.
ask.on_conflict: The chain counts recorded for these sequences disagree. Is each FASTA one complex to fold together, or single chains?
ask.on_absent: not used: with no recorded chain count ColabFold keeps upstream's alphafold2_ptm default

ask.definition: Whether AlphaFold2 folds the FASTA's chains together as one complex (multimer) or one at a time (monomer_ptm); a D.PSEQ with ChainCount 2 or more is a complex.
ask.on_conflict: The chain counts recorded for these sequences disagree. Is each FASTA one complex to fold together, or single chains?
ask.on_absent: not used: with no recorded chain count AlphaFold2 keeps upstream's monomer_ptm default

ask.definition: The platform each library was sequenced on, a required samplesheet column (ENA's instrument_platform vocabulary). taxprofiler uses it to tell long reads (OXFORD_NANOPORE, PACBIO_SMRT) from short reads (every other value), which decides their preprocessing and which databases they meet. A short-read instrument outside the list (Element AVITI, Ultima, Singular, PacBio Onso) is profiled as short reads under ILLUMINA.
ask.on_conflict: This library's sequencer, flow cell and protocol disagree about the platform it was sequenced on. Which is it?
ask.on_absent: Nothing in this library's metadata names a sequencing platform taxprofiler knows. Which was it sequenced on?

ask.definition: Whether each library is DNA (WES/WGS) or RNA; it changes OptiType's configuration.
ask.on_conflict: The sequencing-type label and the sample's own name/files disagree about DNA vs RNA. I won't guess, which is right?
ask.on_absent: Nothing in these samples' metadata says whether they are DNA or RNA libraries. Which are they?

ask.definition: Whether salmon should skip transcript-length correction. A 3' DGE / tag-counting library (QuantSeq, BRB-seq, MARS-seq) sequences only the 3' end, so a transcript's length says nothing about how many reads it should get, and correcting for it biases every fold change. A standard full-length library needs the correction.
ask.on_conflict: The prep protocol and the kit/library fields disagree about whether this is a 3' tag-counting library or a standard full-length RNA library. Which was prepped?
ask.on_absent: not used — rnaseq assumes a standard full-length library and applies length correction

ask.definition: Single-cell chemistry (10x v2/v3/v4 or Drop-seq/Seq-Well). It changes how the aligner parses cell barcodes and UMIs.
ask.on_conflict: The kit fields, the sample name, and the protocol document disagree about the single-cell chemistry. Which was used?
ask.on_absent: I can't tell which single-cell chemistry was used (the exact version isn't recorded). Which chemistry: 10x v2, 10x v3, 10x v4, or Drop-seq?

ask.definition: The 3' adapter to trim off small-RNA reads. Determined by the library prep kit.
ask.on_conflict: The kit fields and the protocol document disagree about the small-RNA kit / 3' adapter. Which kit was used?
ask.on_absent: not used — smrnaseq falls back to the Illumina adapter

ask.definition: The Illumina chemistry each library was sequenced with: 2 (NextSeq, NovaSeq) or 4 (HiSeq, MiSeq). eager trims poly-G tails only on 2-colour data.
ask.on_conflict: The sequencer recorded for these libraries reads both as a 2-colour and a 4-colour instrument. Which was it?
ask.on_absent: not asked: with no instrument recorded eager's own default, 4 (no poly-G trimming), is used

ask.definition: Whether each library was treated with UDG (USER enzyme) to remove deamination damage: full, half (damage left only at the terminal bases) or none. It decides how eager trims and authenticates the reads.
ask.on_conflict: The library type and the protocol disagree about UDG treatment. Was it full, half or none?
ask.on_absent: Nothing in these libraries' metadata says whether they were UDG treated. Was the treatment full, half or none?

ask.definition: Whether each library was built single-stranded or double-stranded; the damage pattern, and so eager's authentication and trimming, differ.
ask.on_conflict: The library type and the protocol disagree about single- or double-stranded library preparation. Which was it?
ask.on_absent: not asked: with nothing recorded the library is double-stranded, eager's own default

ask.definition: Each sample's sex as raredisease's pedigree wants it: 1 male, 2 female, 0 unknown. It drives the X-linked inheritance models and the sex check.
ask.on_conflict: These samples' metadata reads both ways about sex (the Sex field and the sample name disagree). Which is right?
ask.on_absent: Nothing in these samples' metadata records sex. What is each one's sex (male, female or unknown)?

ask.definition: Whether each sample's person is affected by the disease studied: 2 affected, 1 unaffected, 0 not known. raredisease models inheritance from it.
ask.on_conflict: These samples' metadata reads both ways about affected status (for example a carrier, or a Phenotype and a Disease field that disagree). Is each one affected, unaffected or not known?
ask.on_absent: Nothing in these samples' metadata says who is affected. Which samples are affected, and which unaffected?

ask.definition: Whether the libraries are whole genome (wgs) or exome / targeted capture (wes); raredisease limits calling and QC to the kit's targets for wes.
ask.on_conflict: These libraries' metadata reads both as whole genome and as exome or capture. Which are they?
ask.on_absent: Nothing in these libraries' metadata says whole genome or exome. Which are they?

ask.definition: The capture kit's target-region BED, as a path on the cluster. raredisease calls variants and reports coverage only inside it for wes.
ask.on_detect: These look like exome or targeted-capture libraries. Which BED file of the kit's target regions should raredisease use? Give its path on the cluster.

ask.definition: Whether each sample is tumour (1) or normal (0); sarek pairs a patient's tumour with its normal for somatic calling.
ask.on_conflict: The sample's metadata reads both ways about tumour vs normal: a field says something like "non-tumour" or "adjacent", or its tissue type and its own name disagree. I won't guess, which is right?
ask.on_absent: Nothing in these samples' metadata says tumour or normal. Which are tumour?

ask.definition: The capture kit's target-region BED, as a path on the cluster. sarek calls variants only inside it; set wes=true with it.
ask.on_detect: These look like exome or targeted-capture libraries. Which BED file of the kit's target regions should sarek use? Give its path on the cluster.

ask.definition: Whether each library is from the tumour or from the patient's matched normal; oncoanalyser subtracts the normal's germline variants from the tumour's.
ask.on_conflict: The sample's metadata reads both ways about tumour vs normal: a field says something like "non-tumour" or "adjacent", or its tissue type and its own name disagree. I won't guess, which is right?
ask.on_absent: Nothing in these samples' metadata says tumour or normal. Which are tumour?

ask.definition: Whether each library is DNA (whole genome) or RNA (whole transcriptome); oncoanalyser aligns and analyses the two differently, and reads RNA from the tumour only.
ask.on_conflict: The sequencing-type label and the library source or strategy disagree about DNA vs RNA. I won't guess, which is right?
ask.on_absent: Nothing in these samples' metadata says whether they are DNA or RNA libraries. Which are they?

ask.definition: oncoanalyser's mode: wgts for whole-genome DNA and/or whole-transcriptome RNA, targeted for a panel. It has no exome mode, and targeted needs panel resources no run here has.
ask.on_conflict: These libraries' strategy and sequencing type disagree about whole genome vs panel. Which are they?
ask.on_absent: Nothing in these samples' metadata says whole genome, transcriptome or panel. oncoanalyser runs whole-genome/transcriptome (wgts) or a supported panel (targeted), and cannot analyse exome libraries. Which are these?

ask.definition: Each library's strand-specificity, a required samplesheet column. NExtSEEK knows it when an earlier rnaseq run measured it (the D.SEQ Strandedness field), or from a kit whose strand is fixed (dUTP kits such as TruSeq Stranded or NEBNext Ultra II Directional are reverse).
ask.on_conflict: This sample's measured strandedness and its library kit disagree. Which is it: forward, reverse or unstranded?
ask.on_absent: No earlier run measured these libraries' strandedness and their kit does not fix it. Which is it: forward, reverse, unstranded, or unknown if you cannot tell?

ask.definition: Each library's strand-specificity, a required samplesheet column. rnasplice 2.0.0 accepts only forward, reverse or unstranded (no auto), and rMATS needs every sample to share one. NExtSEEK knows it when an earlier rnaseq run measured it (the D.SEQ Strandedness field), or from a kit whose strand is fixed (dUTP kits such as TruSeq Stranded or NEBNext Ultra II Directional are reverse).
ask.on_conflict: This sample's measured strandedness and its library kit disagree. Which is it: forward, reverse or unstranded?
ask.on_absent: No earlier run measured these libraries' strandedness, their kit does not fix it, and rnasplice cannot infer it. Which is it: forward, reverse or unstranded?

ask.definition: Whether each library is ribosome footprints (riboseq), translation-initiation footprints (tiseq) or ordinary RNA-seq of the same samples (rnaseq). It decides which libraries the footprint analyses read and which pair with them for translational efficiency.
ask.on_conflict: This library's sequencing type, library type, protocol and name disagree about whether it is Ribo-seq footprints, TI-seq or ordinary RNA-seq. Which is it?
ask.on_absent: Nothing in this library's metadata says whether it is Ribo-seq footprints, TI-seq or ordinary RNA-seq. Which is it?

ask.definition: Each library's strand-specificity, a required samplesheet column. auto has riboseq infer it with Salmon from a million reads.
ask.on_conflict: This sample's recorded strandedness reads more than one way. Which is it: forward, reverse or unstranded?
ask.on_absent: not used: with no measured strandedness riboseq infers it (auto)

ask.definition: The reads' length; STAR builds its index with read_length - 1 as the splice-junction overhang, so it must match the reads (2x151 reads: 151).
ask.on_conflict: The forward and reverse read lengths recorded for these libraries differ, or differ between libraries. Which read length should STAR's index use?
ask.on_absent: not used: with no recorded read length rnavar keeps its default of 150

ask.definition: The read length atacseq uses to look up the effective genome size for peak calling; the schema takes only 50, 75, 100, 150 or 200, so reads are rounded down (2x151 reads: 150).
ask.on_conflict: The forward and reverse read lengths recorded for these libraries differ, or differ between libraries. Which read length (50, 75, 100, 150 or 200) should peak calling use?
ask.on_absent: No read length is recorded for these libraries, and peak calling needs one to look up the genome size. Which is closest without going over: 50, 75, 100, 150 or 200?

ask.definition: The read length chipseq uses to look up the effective genome size for peak calling; the schema takes only 50, 75, 100, 150 or 200, so reads are rounded down (2x151 reads: 150).
ask.on_conflict: The forward and reverse read lengths recorded for these libraries differ, or differ between libraries. Which read length (50, 75, 100, 150 or 200) should peak calling use?
ask.on_absent: No read length is recorded for these libraries, and peak calling needs one to look up the genome size. Which is closest without going over: 50, 75, 100, 150 or 200?

ask.definition: Whether MACS3 calls narrow peaks (a transcription factor's sharp sites) or its default broad peaks (a histone mark's domains).
ask.on_conflict: These libraries' names, protocols and notes read both ways about whether the target is a histone mark. Is it a histone mark (broad peaks) or a transcription factor (narrow peaks)?
ask.on_absent: Nothing in these libraries' names, protocols or notes names a histone mark. Is the antibody's target a transcription factor (narrow peaks) or a histone mark (broad peaks)? If the cohort holds both, they are best run separately.

ask.definition: The genome of the spike-in DNA that spike-in normalisation counts: E. coli (K12-MG1655, carried over from the enzyme prep), yeast (R64-1-1) or fruit fly (BDGP6) when the protocol added its own.
ask.on_conflict: The protocol and the libraries' notes name different spike-in DNA. Which was added: yeast, fruit fly, or none (E. coli carry-over)?
ask.on_absent: not used: with no added spike-in named, normalisation counts the E. coli DNA carried over from the enzyme prep

ask.definition: Whether the libraries are RRBS (MspI-digested reduced representation). Turns on TrimGalore's RRBS trimming and skips deduplication.
ask.on_conflict: The kit, sequencing type, library and protocol fields read both ways about whether these are RRBS libraries. Which is right?
ask.on_absent: not used: nothing names this prep, so the preset stays off

ask.definition: Whether the libraries are EM-seq (enzymatic conversion). Sets EM-seq's trimming preset and a longer maximum insert for Bismark.
ask.on_conflict: The kit, sequencing type, library and protocol fields read both ways about whether these are EM-seq libraries. Which is right?
ask.on_absent: not used: nothing names this prep, so the preset stays off

ask.definition: Whether the libraries are PBAT (post-bisulfite adapter tagging). Bismark then aligns the complementary strands, and PBAT's trimming preset applies.
ask.on_conflict: The kit, sequencing type, library and protocol fields read both ways about whether these are PBAT libraries. Which is right?

ask.definition: Whether the libraries were made with the Accel-NGS Methyl-Seq kit. Sets its trimming preset.
ask.on_conflict: The kit, sequencing type, library and protocol fields read both ways about whether the Accel-NGS Methyl-Seq kit was used. Which is right?
ask.on_absent: not used: nothing names this prep, so the preset stays off
